positive.prompt: Split this messy working tree into clean atomic commits
Resolve the merge conflict on this feature branch
How should we tag and version this release?
Commit this work and open a pull request

negative.prompt: Add a loading spinner to the submit button
Write integration tests for the payments API
Review this pull request for correctness before we merge it

evals.prompt: The working tree mixes a refactor, a bug fix, and a new feature. Turn it into a clean history.
evals.expected_output: Separate atomic commits with clear messages, each independently green
expectations: Refactor, fix, and feature land as separate commits
Commit messages are imperative and standalone
Each commit leaves the tree in a working state
The staged and unstaged diff is inspected before splitting; existing work is not discarded with reset --hard or clean
The rounding fix and CSV feature each include acceptance tests in their behavior commit
Each committed tree is verified with actual focused checks rather than relying on the final combined working tree

evals.prompt: Use the supplied app.js and app.test.js to rehearse a merge conflict locally. Create two isolated branches whose total changes conflict: one rounds currency, one extracts sumPrices. Merge them preserving both behaviors and original assertions; add a rounding regression test. Do not push or discard unrelated work. Verify the resolved commit tree.
evals.expected_output: A real locally resolved conflict preserving helper extraction and rounding, with passing focused tests and preserved baseline coverage
expectations: The executor actually creates and resolves a local conflict using base and both branch versions
The resolved total extracts or calls the helper and rounds currency; baseline assertions remain
A rounding regression check runs and passes on the resolved commit tree
No external push or destructive dirty-tree reset is performed
